title: Kummer tower and low-degree comparison for a strict local regular divisor
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a strictly henselian regular local ring with $\ell$ invertible, and let $f\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor such that $R/(f)$ is regular. Here strictly henselian means henselian with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and regularity is [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Set $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $D=V(f)$, $U=S\setminus D$, and
$$S_r=\operatorname{Spec}R[t_r]/(t_r^{\ell^r}-f),\quad U_r=S_r\setminus V(t_r)\quad(r\geq0),$$
where $t_r\mapsto t_{r+1}^{\ell}$ defines the transitions and $U_0=U$; affine spectra and polynomial rings are [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Put $G=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r}(R)$ with transition $z\mapsto z^\ell$ and the inverse-limit topology. This is a procyclic group isomorphic to the additive topological group $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Write $BG$ for the topos of discrete continuous $G$-sets, and its $A$-module objects as discrete continuous $A[G]$-modules [def-exc-discrete-modules-category]. A morphism of topoi means an adjunction whose inverse image preserves finite limits; derived sections on $BG$ mean derived invariants [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]. Use the small-etale site and cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and ordinary bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The connected finite etale torsors $U_r\to U$ define a morphism of topoi $\rho_f:U_{\mathrm{et}}\to BG$. For $q=0,1$ its pullback maps
$$H^q(BG,A)\longrightarrow H^q(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$$
are isomorphisms. With $g':BG\to BG$ induced by multiplication by $\ell$ on $G$, $g:U_1\to U$ the first cover and $\rho_{t_1}:U_{1,\mathrm{et}}\to BG$ defined by the shifted root tower, the square $g'\rho_{t_1}=\rho_fg$ is cartesian up to its canonical topos isomorphism. More explicitly, for $Q=G/\ell G$, $U_{1,\mathrm{et}}\simeq U_{\mathrm{et}}/\rho_f^*Q$ and $BG\simeq(BG)/Q$ on the top right, with the latter equivalence identifying $G$ with $\ell G$ by multiplication by $\ell$.
